instructions: Open book. Answer each item from the saved AWS pages and the fact canon only. Give citations for every label: why the key is right and why each other option is wrong. A citation is a fact id or {source_id, quote} with a verbatim quote. Set flag when a second answer is defensible, else null.

items.stem: A company has one AWS account and does not use AWS Organizations. The company plans to keep this single-account setup. The company runs AWS Managed Microsoft AD in a VPC for its Windows workloads, and its ten administrators have user accounts in this directory. The administrators must use the AWS Management Console with their directory credentials. The company wants to avoid IAM users. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.label: A
options.text: Create an IAM user for each administrator with the same name and password as in the directory, and require MFA for each IAM user.

options.label: B
options.text: Create an access URL for the directory, assign an IAM role to the directory group of the administrators, and let them sign in at that URL.

options.label: C
options.text: Enable an account instance of IAM Identity Center in the account, connect the directory, and assign permission sets to the administrators' group.

options.label: D
options.text: Run AD FS on Amazon EC2 instances joined to the directory, create a SAML identity provider and IAM roles in the account, and federate the administrators.
